title: Prove which store file SQLite actually holds, so a recovered Engram control child can be matched to TermAl's pinned store (required for TermAl Unknown recovery)
outcome: control_connection_read returns the canonical path of the store file SQLite actually holds, proven at handle level, on every supported platform. TermAl's Unknown-outcome recovery (TermAl w-decd R4) can then match a recovered child to its pinned store, instead of leaving it GAP.
acceptance: On a current serving connection (original or resumed), control_connection_read returns the canonical database_path of the file SQLite itself holds, proven by SQLite's own handle-level check: SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED on Unix; on Windows the SQLite-held handle with GetFinalPathNameByHandle and a 128-bit FILE_ID_INFO identity, safe on ReFS. It refuses with control_connection_identity_unavailable whenever that proof is unavailable or fails, and never returns a possibly different file.
Any unsafe code is limited to that single proof function, under an explicit exception Greg approves (Cargo.toml currently sets unsafe_code = "forbid"); no other unsafe is introduced.

Tests cover: a proven match on each platform; a swap or restore of the file, a parent junction or symlink, and a moved file each causing a refusal; and the read changing no state and needing no grant.
The protocol docs replace the fail-closed-only contract from w-e96f37a1f665 with this proven contract, with no wire-shape change.
